title: Build a two-site VCF 9.1 architecture and migration artifact
prompt:
Build the production architecture artifact for the Northstar Retail VMware Cloud Foundation transition. This is an architecture deliverable, not an explanatory report.

The immutable inputs are `fixtures/design_requirements.json`, `fixtures/estate_inventory.json`, `fixtures/compatibility_snapshot.json`, `schemas/architecture-artifact.schema.json`, and the VCF Installer 9.1 schema at `specifications/vcf-installer/vcf-installer-openapi.json`. The installer file is the `specifications/vcf-installer/vcf-installer-openapi.json` file from tag `9.1.0.0` of the Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository. Leave all of those files, `.protected/verify.py`, and the bundled license unchanged.

Before implementing, use the harness's real network research capabilities to consult Broadcom's currently reachable, published compatibility, product-interoperability, upgrade-path, lifecycle, and VCF 9.1 upgrade material. Make genuine fetches; do not treat the pinned snapshot as a substitute for live research. Choose the sources and searches yourself. Record what you actually consulted in `research.json`. It must contain a top-level `consulted` array of source objects, each with string fields `title`, `url`, `retrieved_at`, and `finding`, plus a nonempty string array named `topics`; it must also contain a top-level string array named `snapshot_discrepancies`. Use the topic values `compatibility`, `product-interoperability`, `upgrade-path`, `lifecycle`, and `vcf-9.1-upgrade` to identify which requested areas each consulted source informed, and cover all five areas across the log. Do not invent a source you did not fetch. Live publications can change, so use `fixtures/compatibility_snapshot.json` as the artifact's pinned compatibility authority and record any live discrepancy rather than changing the pinned result.

Implement a Python package named `vcf_architecture` using only the Python standard library. It must expose a CLI with this interface:

`python3 -m vcf_architecture --requirements fixtures/design_requirements.json --inventory fixtures/estate_inventory.json --compatibility fixtures/compatibility_snapshot.json --output architecture.json`

The command must deterministically build `architecture.json` from those three inputs and overwrite the requested output. It must reject malformed input with a nonzero exit. Do not add runtime dependencies.

The generated `architecture.json` must conform to `schemas/architecture-artifact.schema.json`. Its `greenfield.sddc_spec` must be an `SddcSpec` under the bundled VCF Installer OpenAPI document and must express the primary-site greenfield VCF 9.1 management domain, including the stated hosts, networks, management-domain design choices, vSAN resilience, NSX managers, three-node Operations deployment, VCF Management Services address pool/internal CIDR, SDDC Manager, and license server. The two-site portion must size primary and recovery workload domains from demand, headroom, host capacity, and failure tolerance; the 18 ms site RTT requires separate VCF instances and non-stretched clusters.

The existing-estate portion must be an ordered migration plan. Include every inventory component exactly once, preserving its exact current version, and give each component's target component, target version, disposition, full supported path, actions, and technical gates. Follow the pinned rule order and compatibility facts. In particular, do not invent a direct upgrade across the Aria Automation support boundary, do not treat the standalone Logs appliance as an in-place 9.1 upgrade, and retain the mandated core ordering through the final NSX Edge step.

Commit the generated `architecture.json` alongside the package and `research.json`. Acceptance is `python3 -B .protected/verify.py`.
